correctness.rationale: A nonempty face contains at most one color per layer, so no such face can be invariant and no geometric point is fixed. The ordinary quotient is a finite CW complex and agrees up to homotopy with the Borel construction. Thapper Proposition 3.2 gives the three stated covering homotopy types, with d≥2 for m≥4. For a single odd sphere the top rank-one module is trivial, and the two rows are copies of Z[u]/(3u). If the transgression of the top generator were zero, u-linearity would leave unbounded bottom-row cohomology. It is therefore a unit mod 3, killing the positive-column top row and the high bottom row, with kernel 3Z on the top generator. For the pair of even spheres the Lefschetz trace of a generator on the top is −1, forcing characteristic polynomial T²+T+1, zero norm, no invariants and determinant of g−1 equal to 3. The integral periodic resolution gives Z/3 exactly in odd positive columns of the top row, where multiplication by u gives the period isomorphism. The same finite-dimensionality argument forces the differential out of column 1 to be an isomorphism there and in all odd columns. Thus in the even case only H^0 and the bottom even classes through degree d survive; in the odd case the bottom even classes through degree d−1 and top Z survive. There is at most one surviving filtration piece per total degree. The integral UCT recovers the specified groups and no others, including the asserted torsion orders. Independent Smith-form computations for m=4,5,6, using layer subsets with the first selected color normalized to zero, gave respectively only H1=Z/3; H1=Z/3 and H3=Z; and H1=Z/3 and H3=Z in positive degrees, as predicted.
residual_risks: The finite replay covers m=4,5,6 only and is supplemental; the integral proof covers all m≥4. No multiplicative cohomology or lens-space homotopy type is inferred. The broken typography in the floor notation is read as k=⌊m/3⌋ as fixed by the three residue cases.

value.rationale: The simultaneous color quotient of this standard infinite family is natural, and the entire quotient integral homology is useful beyond the previously identified π1 or cover Betti numbers. It identifies the distinction between lens-space homology and rational acyclicity with arbitrarily long integral torsion ladders, including the terminal and high-degree information not supplied by low-degree group homology alone. The use of standard tools does not reduce the complete even-residue computation to a change of parameters in an inspected result.
residual_risks: The result gives additive integral homology only; it does not establish a homotopy-type distinction beyond what this invariant detects.
